# Was personal data exposed, does this start a GDPR breach assessment or a 72-hour notification, and what do I document?

M
The answer in thirty seconds

A flaw is not a breach. An unpatched, internet-facing PHP application holding personal data is a risk to record and treat; it becomes a breach to assess when there is a sign of compromise on it. No named organisation has said it was compromised through php2shell as of the last check. Ask your hosts in writing, review from 17 October, and document the assessment either way.

Read the site as Morgan →

Four questions, in order: is personal data on a system that was exposed, has anything happened to it, does that make it a personal data breach, and what goes on the record. A vulnerability is not a breach, and an outage you chose is not one either; a sign that someone ran code on a system holding personal data is where the assessment starts. Written by the GRC desk; the full register is at GRC.

## What to decide or do
- **Find the personal data first.** Ask the CTO or security lead for the list of internet-facing PHP systems (vendor products and hosting panels count), and mark which hold or reach personal data: accounts, orders, case files, the database the application logs into. Code execution on the server gives an attacker what the PHP process can read, usually including the database credentials in its configuration.
- **Exposed is not breached.** An unpatched system is a risk under Article 32 to treat and record, not a breach under Article 33. As of the last check, no named organisation has said it was compromised through php2shell; attempts are widely reported and two vendors report successful exploitation without naming a victim. What that statement rests on.
- **When the 72-hour clock starts.** Under Article 33 it runs from when you become aware, with reasonable certainty, that personal data was affected: a web shell, a PHP worker spawning a shell, an unexplained database export on a system holding personal data. Ask the security lead to tell you the hour that happens, not the day after, and start the assessment then.
- **A precautionary shutdown is a decision, not a breach.** Taking a service offline on purpose to protect it is not an accidental or unlawful loss of availability. Record who decided, when, for how long, and that no personal data was lost.
- **Ask your processors in writing.** A host or managed platform is a processor under Article 28 and must tell you of a breach without undue delay (Article 33(2)). Ask each one: have you updated PHP on the systems that process our data, since when, have you seen any sign of compromise, and will you tell us within hours if you do? Keep the replies.
- **Document either way.** Article 33(5) asks you to record every breach; accountability under Article 5(2) asks you to show your reasoning when you decide something is not one. Record: the systems and the personal data on each, the date each was patched or isolated, the log review window (from 17 October, the earliest reported attempt, not from the 21st), what was found, and the decision with its reasons and who made it.
- **If it becomes a breach.** Notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to people (Article 33), and tell the people affected without undue delay if the risk to them is high (Article 34). Coordinate with whoever owns the NIS2 or DORA report: the same incident can start a 24-hour clock there.

The list now draws on more captured reports (Germany's hospitals and hosts, Morocco, Romania, Japan), but most are press accounts; few come from the organisations themselves (the Dutch government, Latvia's agency, Weird Gloop, the Charité's spokesman as quoted). A community tracker counts 51 listed and 50 back.
- Whether the 8.5.12 fix is complete. A Fediverse report of a third bug or incomplete fix reached oss-security on 21 October; PHP reportedly told Canonical it is unrelated. On 23 October PHP published an informational advisory for a separate flaw, CVE-2026-115560, in the session upload progress feature, reported by Cloudflare, SOCRadar and The Hacker News: it affects fully patched releases including 8.5.12, needs a rare session setting, will be fixed in the next regular release, and has session.upload_progress.enabled=0 as the mitigation; SOCRadar reports no exploitation and no severity score. PHP's advisory is not in the evidence vault, and whether this is the bug the Fediverse report described is not stated.

## The line

php2shell is a severe flaw that, two days after its release, still has no confirmed victim. The story has moved from the bug to the second stories: who is still exposed, who ships the fix, and what the devices in front of servers are made of. The evidence for every line below is in the evidence vault, now refreshed to 227 sources, and in the source watch's dated series.

## Compromise: still none confirmed, three cases open

No named organisation has confirmed a compromise through php2shell. As the researcher's evidence page puts it, that is "a time-bounded absence, not a confirmed fact": true as of the last check, and one statement would end it; the rows behind it are on the compromise evidence page. The PHP Foundation knows of no successful remote code execution; Dataminr sees scanning, fingerprinting and non-working exploits. WIRED BleepingComputer Four named incidents have been linked to php2shell in the press, and none holds yet.

- **Valtec** in Japan blamed the PHP flaw for a service halt, then corrected itself the same day: the flaw was in its own service. Ruled out. INTERNET Watch

- **ČVUT**, the Czech Technical University, says it stopped an attack that it calls part of the worldwide attempts against PHP sites. That is an attack, in the organisation's words, not a confirmed compromise. Open. Lupa.cz

- **GMO**'s FX trading VPS service found unauthorised programs on some servers on 20 October, the day of the leak and before the release; up to 26,739 servers may be affected. GMO names no cause. Open, and timing is not attribution. Yahoo! News Japan

- **DMM** halted services for a vulnerability "in external software" and will not confirm PHP. Open. 産経ニュース

One more claim is unverified: a startup owner told Fortune that source code was stolen through the bug. Fortune Patchstack says hosting partners reported "multiple active exploitation incidents" before the release, without naming any. Recorded Future Headlines in WIRED and The Verge say "exploited"; their bodies describe attempts. WIRED The Verge

## Exploitation and weaponisation

Attempts are broad. Amazon calls it "broadly exploited in the wild" and adds that it is unclear whether any attempt would have worked; Hadrian says exploitation is at scale, mostly through PHP's session upload-progress mechanism; VulnCheck saw at least one Chinese IP address try, and fail, to deploy a webshell. SecurityWeek The Register National authorities in Germany, Switzerland and Japan say, as reported, that they know of no successful exploitation, joining the US and Australia. RTL.de Watson 共同網 CISA ACSC

The markers of weaponisation have not moved: neither CVE is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog at the last check, 08:03 UTC today, and no Metasploit module has been merged. CISA EPSS puts the chance of exploitation activity in the next 30 days at about 5%, near the 93rd percentile. NIST has now analysed both records and added its own CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8 beside the PHP project's CVSS 4.0 9.2, so a reader will meet both numbers. NVD NVD Public GitHub repositories matching "php2shell" went from 586 to 735 overnight; that is search results, not working exploits.

## Patching: the fix is reaching servers, and the tail is end-of-life

The NCSC-NL inventory, read from its public history, had 109 of 751 products fixed at 12:50 UTC today, against 46 of 674 when the vault captured it yesterday morning; the pile under investigation fell from 418 to 389, and 30 products are now marked not affected. NCSC-NL The newly fixed include Azure App Service, AWS Elastic Beanstalk, SUSE, NixOS and Synology's PHP packages back to 7.4. The hour-by-hour curve is on the inventory page.

The tail is the number the patching story lacked yesterday. VirusTotal's analysis, as reported, finds about 5.1 million IPs running PHP; of the 1.1 million that disclose a version, about 758,000 run an end-of-life branch and about 272,000 a supported one. TugaTech Recorded Future Most of the exposed population is on versions the PHP project did not release a fix for.

## The protection layer is in scope

Ten products from security and network vendors are now marked vulnerable in the inventory: Palo Alto's PAN-OS and Panorama, Check Point's firewall web interfaces, NetScaler ADC and Gateway, two parts of F5's BIG-IP, Cisco's Expressway series and URWB, and Sophos's MyUTM portal. Palo Alto confirms PAN-OS 10.2 to 12.2 are affected through the management interface, with fixes pending and no exploitation known to it. Palo Alto Networks Cisco's advisory as captured on 22 October knew of no affected product; the inventory now marks three, which is a change over time, not a contradiction. Cisco

A community tracker lists 51 sites that went dark over php2shell; 50 are back, and French prefecture websites are the one still dark. PHPocalypse Tracker The Dutch government's DigiD, MijnOverheid and Overheid.nl are back online. Security.NL

## The line

Two and a half days after the release, php2shell still has no confirmed victim, and the story is now about what comes after the patch. The evidence vault holds 295 sources, 68 more than this desk's last version, most of them coverage from 21 and 22 October in a dozen languages, selected mechanically and read by the curator. They add detail and new countries; they do not add a victim.

## Compromise: none confirmed, and the question changes

No named organisation has confirmed a compromise through php2shell, at the vault's latest capture, 16:04 UTC on 23 October. The three named cases that were open in version 1 (ČVUT, GMO and DMM) are still open, and no new source changes any of them. Lupa.cz Yahoo! News Japan 産経ニュース

In Luxembourg, Paperjam reports that no financial institution, public service or operator has announced an intrusion, and that the authorities ask operators to search back for traces of compromise and to keep the evidence. Paperjam Singapore's Cyber Security Agency tells organisations to patch internet-facing systems first and to investigate whether they may already have been compromised. CNA IT Social's headline on 23 October is the turn in one line: the update closes the flaw, but obliges a hunt for possible compromises; its body adds that the published figures measure attempts, not successful intrusions. IT Social

That is the right next question, and it is a slower one. A patch is visible from outside; a break-in is found only by the operator who looks for it. The absence of a named victim is therefore weaker evidence each day that operators have not yet looked.

## Exploitation: attempts in millions, weaponisation unchanged

Cloudflare's count, as its chief executive put it, went from thousands of attempts in the ten hours before the announcement to millions by early on 22 October; attempts, not intrusions. Matthew Prince, Cloudflare CEO on… GinjFo AhnLab, as reported, examined 100 GitHub repositories related to php2shell on 22 October and classed 27 as proof-of-concept exploits. 合同会社ロケットボーイズ This desk has not opened any of them, and will not.

One source contradicts another about Patchstack. Recorded Future reports that Patchstack received reports of "multiple active exploitation incidents" from hosting partners by 07:34 UTC on 21 October; PCMag quotes Patchstack saying that, shortly after the update, its telemetry showed "only probing attacks, with no hard evidence of breaches yet". Recorded Future PCMag Both can be true at different times and of different things, reports received and telemetry seen, but neither names a victim.

The markers of weaponisation have not moved: neither CVE was in the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog at the old source watch's last check, 08:03 UTC on 23 October, and no Metasploit module had been merged. CISA This desk does not yet read the source watch's new vault, so that check is now sixteen hours old; the next version will say what it shows.

Risikomonitor examined nearly 690,000 servers linked to Switzerland on 22 October and found just over 23,000, about 3.5%, still affected; it says the real number may be higher because the PHP version cannot always be read. ICTjournal It is the first count in the vault of what remains after the fix in one country, and it sits beside VirusTotal's global picture, as reported, of about 758,000 end-of-life servers among the 1.1 million that disclose a version. TugaTech The two do not measure the same thing: one counts servers still affected in one country, the other counts versions anywhere.

The NCSC-NL inventory has not changed since 12:50 UTC on 23 October: 109 of 751 products fixed, 389 under investigation. NCSC-NL

More national authorities are in the record. Peru's Centro Nacional de Seguridad Digital called php2shell a critical threat in its report of 21 October. Agencia Andina Morocco's DGSSI issued a critical bulletin the same day. ## What this version does not say, and why

The curator flagged six claims for checking against the ledger. This desk checked each against the saved page and the site's claims and contradiction records, and holds them back as worded:

- **That Japan's Prime Minister issued an emergency order.** One Vietnamese outlet says so. nguoiquansat.vn Reuters, CNN and USA Today, in the vault, describe Sanae Takaichi urging website operators, on X, to check whether their sites use PHP and to prepare to patch, and, in CNN's account, saying companies should consider suspending services if necessary: a request, not an order. rte.ie CNN USA Today

- **That exploitation is "confirmed" on WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, phpMyAdmin, Nextcloud and Magento.** Help Net Security does not say who confirmed it. - **That the bug was first spotted in the wild in 2024.** Mashable India gives no source. Mashable India The earliest attempt in the record is Amazon's, on 17 October 2026. Cyber Press A 2024 audit by Quarkslab did find the out-of-memory issue without proving it exploitable, which may be where a 2024 date comes from. PHP Foundation

Which versions are affected is already an explained contradiction on the fact-check desk; nobody in the vault names the commit that introduced the flaw.

## Exploitation: on CISA's list

CISA's alert of 26 October says it "has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog": CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The catalog's version 2026.10.26, released at 22:24 UTC on 26 October and captured by the newsroom at 00:45 UTC on 27 October, lists both with the date added 26 October, a due date of 29 October and known ransomware use "Unknown". CISA CISA CISA

What it establishes: CISA holds evidence that the flaws are exploited. The alert says an addition "must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance". CISA It supersedes CISA's alert of 21 October, which said it "has not observed exploitation of these vulnerabilities as of the time of publication", so the US leaves the count of authorities that know of no successful exploitation, which falls from six to five. CISA The due date binds only US federal civilian agencies under BOD 26-04; the alert encourages every organisation to prioritise the catalog. "Unknown" in the ransomware field is the catalog's value, neither a finding of ransomware use nor a finding that there is none. CISA CISA

The last PHP core flaw, CVE-2024-4577, was listed three days after disclosure; this one was listed five days after the fixes of 21 October. Akamai Security Research CISA
